source.title: Learning to Teach with Deep Interactions
source.authors: Yang Fan; Yingce Xia; Lijun Wu; Shufang Xie; Wei-Qing Liu; Jiang Bian; Tao Qin; Xiang-Yang Li; Tie-Yan Liu

record.file_problem: The supplied text is the full paper, though the beginning of Section 5.2's table is disrupted in the extraction; the table values and headings remain identifiable from the surrounding text.
record.tranche_reason: The paper reports results on CIFAR with corrupted training labels, a different method and measure from the original random-label experiments. It reports test error, not training error or whether the networks fit the noisy labels.
record.gate_note: The noisy-label experiments bear on V4, but report test error only. The clean-label results, feature ablations, and translation results do not test the claim versions. Results cited from other studies are not extracted.
record.test_reason: The study evaluates a data-reweighting method using clean-test error under label corruption. It reports no training error, memorization rate, or learning trajectories. These mitigation-performance results do not establish random-label fitting or the joint training-fit and test-error behavior in V4. The record's tests/T2 classification should be corrected.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the authors conclude that using student internal states for jointly learned data reweighting improves image classification and translation performance in clean and noisy settings. They draw no conclusion about fitting random labels.
record.recipe_differences: The study jointly trains a teacher model that reweights examples and a student model using validation feedback; the claim concerns standard network training without changing the training setup.
record.method_sensitivity: Noise type, corruption probability, dataset, student architecture, and reweighting method vary across the noisy-label experiments.

fits_no_version.finding: Table 5 reports higher baseline test error when uniform corruption increases from 40% to 60%: 31.93% to 46.88% on CIFAR-10 and 48.89% to 69.08% on CIFAR-100. Reweighting reduces these errors, but training-set fit is unreported.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: At the tested uniform-corruption rates, greater label corruption worsens clean-test performance, and learned reweighting improves robustness.

fits_no_version.finding: Table 6 reports higher baseline test error when flip noise increases from 20% to 40%: 23.17% to 29.23% on CIFAR-10 and 49.14% to 56.99% on CIFAR-100. The proposed method lowers these errors to 8.95%/11.29% and 33.92%/39.49%, respectively.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Learned data reweighting improves clean-test performance under the tested class-dependent label corruption.

record.problems: No training-error results are reported for the noisy-label experiments, so the paper does not establish whether the networks fit the corrupted training sets. The tested corruption rates do not span clean labels through fully random labels. No uncertainty estimates are reported.
record.rows_left_out: No eligible rows: the noisy-label tables report test errors, but the claim version V4 requires training-set fit as well as test-error behavior. The text does not report training error for these conditions.

untested.parts: Fitting completely random labels to near-zero training error, chance test performance, and unchanged architecture and training hyperparameters.
Relative training time and convergence speed for true versus random labels, including dependence on corruption fraction.
Training-set fitting of shuffled pixels, independently permuted pixels, and Gaussian-noise inputs.

Perfect training-set fit as corruption increases, degradation across the clean-to-fully-random range, and simultaneous signal learning and noise memorization. Selected-rate test errors alone cannot establish this behavior.
Whether weight decay, dropout, or augmentation prevent random-label fitting, and whether removing them harms clean-label generalization.
Whether real patterns precede noise memorization and how real versus random labels are learned over training.

record.verdict_notes: The empty row set is appropriate for these claim versions. The omitted noisy-label test-error results are already declared in rows_left_out; they do not warrant V4 verdicts without evidence of training-set fitting.

versions.untested_parts: Completely random labeling, training error, test error at chance, and unchanged architecture and hyperparameters.
Training time or convergence speed as label corruption increases.
Shuffled pixels, independently permuted pixels, and Gaussian-noise inputs.

The study varies corruption among selected nonzero rates, but does not test clean through fully random labels as a sweep. It reports test error but not training error, so whether training error stays perfect cannot be determined.
Whether regularization, dropout, or augmentation affect fitting random labels or generalization on true labels.
Whether real patterns are learned before noisy or random labels, or whether the two are learned differently over training.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
